name: Burgruine Thaur
kurzbeschreibung: The romantic castle ruin of Thaur above the Inn Valley features the charming Romedikirchl chapel, historic castle cellars, and glorious Karwendel panoramas.
beschreibung:
Overview

The legendary Thaur Castle Ruins (Burgruine Thaur) crown a sunny forest terrace at the base of the Nordkette range high above the Inn Valley near the village of Thaur. Originally established during the 12th century as one of the largest and strongest fortification complexes in the Tyrolean Inn Valley, the citadel served the Counts of Andechs and later Tyrolean territorial princes as a strategic stronghold controlling the salt trade and river transport. Following severe earthquakes and fires in the 16th century, the fortress decayed into ruins; today, the historic stone walls alongside the picturesque Romedikirchl chapel form a widely visible cultural landmark and popular hiking destination.

Route & Requirements

From the idyllic village center of Thaur, a meditative pilgrimage trail lined with traditional wayside shrine stations ascends in gentle switchbacks through pine woods up the mountain slopes. Reaching the summit, visitors can explore the exposed foundation walls of the outer bailey, the cavernous vaulted castle cellar, and the distinctive open-air amphitheater that regularly hosts the celebrated Thaur Castle Theater plays. Directly adjacent to the stone ruins, the baroque Romedikirchl welcomes guests with delicate Wessobrunn stucco and votive tablets for contemplation and rest. From the observation terrace, the Inn Valley spreads out panoramic vistas from Innsbruck to Hall in Tirol. The trail is a gravel forest path suitable for families with casual walking footwear.

Visit & Arrival

The outdoor castle grounds are open freely at all times throughout the year free of charge. The Romedikirchl chapel opens during daytime on summer weekends. Public transit connections are very convenient: VVT regional bus lines link Innsbruck and Hall in Tirol every fifteen minutes with the Thaur Volksschule stop, followed by a pleasant thirty-minute uphill walk to the ruins. Drivers follow the Dörferstraße to Thaur and utilize the dedicated hikers' car park located above the shooting range at the edge of the forest.

Tips

Especially during springtime fruit blossom or on crisp golden autumn days, the ruin's lookout terrace provides an unforgettable panorama across the valley to the snow-covered Stubai glaciers. Stop at the traditional Gasthof Romediwirt inn right beside the ruins, where savory Tyrolean dumplings, cold platters, and refreshments are served on a large scenic sun deck.
preis: Free access to the ruins and chapel (contributions toward heritage preservation welcome)
oeffnungszeiten: Grounds accessible year-round during daylight; Romedikirchl open on weekends in summer
